articles.headline: Detectado en Chantada el primer caso de lengua azul del serotipo 3 en Lugo
articles.subtitle: Un bovino de una explotación de Chantada ha dado positivo por el serotipo 3 de la lengua azul, el primer caso oficial de esa variante en la provincia de Lugo, y la Xunta recuerda que la vacunación es voluntaria.
articles.body:
La Consellería de Medio Rural ha confirmado el primer caso oficial de lengua azul del serotipo 3 en la provincia de Lugo. El positivo corresponde a un bovino de una explotación de Chantada y fue verificado por el Laboratorio Central de Veterinaria de Algete, según informaron El Progreso y La Voz de Galicia.

Es el cuarto caso de esta variante en Galicia en 2026, tras los tres detectados en julio entre Lugo y A Coruña; el anterior caso provincial correspondía al serotipo 8. La detección se produjo gracias a la vigilancia pasiva del propio ganadero, que alertó ante los primeros síntomas.

La Xunta recuerda que la vacunación frente al serotipo 3 sigue siendo voluntaria para el ganado bovino y ovino, y que la enfermedad se transmite por la picadura de mosquitos del género Culicoides. Las autoridades piden a los titulares de explotaciones que extremen la vigilancia y comuniquen cualquier sospecha al servicio veterinario oficial.

articles.headline: Una mujer muere en un accidente de tres vehículos en el corredor Sarria-Lugo
articles.subtitle: Una mujer ha fallecido y nueve personas han resultado heridas, dos de ellas graves, en una colisión de tres vehículos en el corredor CG-2.2 a su paso por O Corgo, que obligó a cortar la vía en ambos sentidos.
articles.body:
Una mujer ha muerto y nueve personas han resultado heridas, dos de ellas de gravedad, en una colisión entre tres vehículos registrada este viernes por la tarde en el corredor CG-2.2 a la altura de Anseán, en el municipio de O Corgo, en dirección a Monforte. Uno de los turismos volcó tras el impacto.

El 112 Galicia movilizó al 061, a los bomberos de Sarria y a la Guardia Civil de Tráfico, y un helicóptero medicalizado evacuó a uno de los heridos. El accidente obligó a cortar la circulación entre la rotonda de Nadela y la salida 10 en dirección a Maceda, con desvíos por la N-547.

La Guardia Civil mantiene abierta una investigación para esclarecer las causas del siniestro, mientras los servicios de emergencia trabajaron durante horas para atender a los afectados y retirar los vehículos implicados.

articles.headline: Rescatados cuatro perros con sarna y mutilaciones de una casa okupada de Lugo
articles.subtitle: La Policía Local de Lugo y los servicios municipales han rescatado a cuatro perros con signos de sarna y mutilaciones que se encontraban en una casa okupada de la rúa Lavandeira, según El Progreso y La Voz de Galicia.
articles.body:
Cuatro perros con evidentes signos de sarna y mutilaciones han sido rescatados de una casa okupada en la rúa Lavandeira de Lugo. Los animales, que presentaban cortes y afecciones en la piel, fueron localizados por la Policía Local tras el aviso de los vecinos, en una vivienda que llevaba tiempo ocupada.

Las imágenes difundidas por los servicios municipales muestran a los animales en mal estado, con zonas de piel sin pelo y heridas visibles. Tras el rescate, los perros fueron trasladados para recibir atención veterinaria y algunos quedaron a cargo de la protectora de animales de la ciudad.

Desde el Concello recuerdan la importancia de denunciar las situaciones de abandono y maltrato animal, y avanzan que se investigará la situación de la vivienda para determinar las responsabilidades.

articles.headline: El Gobierno sondeó al Rey sobre la oportunidad de llamar a Mohamed VI por Ceuta
articles.subtitle: Moncloa consultó a la Casa Real si era conveniente que Felipe VI llamara a Mohamed VI para tratar la crisis migratoria de Ceuta, pero la llamada no llegó a producirse por temor a que se malinterpretara, según El País.
articles.body:
El Gobierno consultó a la Casa Real si era oportuno que Felipe VI llamara a Mohamed VI para intentar desactivar la crisis desatada por la entrada masiva de migrantes en Ceuta, según publica El País. La llamada, sin embargo, no llegó a producirse: la Casa Real consideró que podría malinterpretarse públicamente en un contexto en el que la crisis sigue lejos de superarse.

Los monarcas no mantienen la relación personal que sí tuvieron Juan Carlos I y Hasán II. Felipe VI recibió esta semana en Palma al presidente de Ceuta, Juan Vivas, y ha telefoneado a Sánchez, al presidente ceutí y a Feijóo, mientras Moncloa valora una visita del Rey a la ciudad autónoma cuando sea útil y razonable.

El Gobierno, por su parte, agradeció públicamente la cooperación de Marruecos en la gestión de la emergencia y trabaja en el traslado de los menores no acompañados a la península, que el Ejecutivo considera factible en pocas semanas.

articles.headline: Marruecos insiste en que Ceuta y Melilla son un derecho histórico y España responde
articles.subtitle: El ministro de Justicia marroquí, Abdellatif Ouahbi, ha insistido en que Ceuta y Melilla constituyen un derecho histórico y geográfico de Marruecos, mientras Exteriores recuerda que ambas ciudades son españolas.
articles.body:
El ministro de Justicia de Marruecos, Abdellatif Ouahbi, ha vuelto a reivindicar que Ceuta y Melilla constituyen un derecho histórico y geográfico de su país, en plena crisis por la entrada masiva de migrantes en la ciudad autónoma.

En declaraciones recogidas por RTVE y Europa Press, Ouahbi insistió en la reclamación marroquí y defendió que la solución pasa por el diálogo, en un momento en el que Rabat reclama también el traslado de los menores no acompañados.

El Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores español respondió con contundencia que Ceuta y Melilla son españolas y que su soberanía no se negocia, rechazando cualquier cuestionamiento. La reivindicación se produce además cuando el Gobierno español ha agradecido la cooperación marroquí en la gestión de la emergencia, y mientras el PP critica la gestión de Sánchez y del Ministerio del Interior.

articles.headline: El incendio de Las Hurdes evoluciona favorablemente y los evacuados regresan a casa
articles.subtitle: El incendio forestal declarado en Pinofranqueado, en Las Hurdes, evoluciona de forma favorable y permite ya el regreso de varios vecinos a sus casas y el desconfinamiento de algunas alquerías, con 4.250 hectáreas afectadas.
articles.body:
El incendio forestal de Pinofranqueado, que ha calcinado la comarca cacereña de Las Hurdes, evoluciona de forma favorable y permite el regreso de varios vecinos a sus casas, el desconfinamiento de algunas alquerías y el restablecimiento del suministro eléctrico, según RTVE.

La superficie afectada se revisa a la baja: de las 4.800 hectáreas iniciales se pasa a unas 4.250. El dispositivo mantiene la situación 2 de Infocaex, con 163 efectivos sobre el terreno, y vigila los focos activos al norte de El Gasco, en el límite con Castilla y León.

El vicepresidente de la Junta de Extremadura, Abel Bautista, presidió la reunión del Cecopi en la que se acordó permitir la vuelta de los evacuados. Las alquerías de Aceitunilla, Erías y Cerezal quedaron desconfinadas, aunque las autoridades piden prudencia y recuerdan que el fuego aún no está estabilizado.

articles.headline: Desarticuladas dos redes que llevaban migrantes de Ceuta a la península por 9.000 euros
articles.subtitle: La Policía Nacional ha detenido a cinco personas vinculadas a dos organizaciones dedicadas al tráfico ilícito de migrantes entre Ceuta y la península, que cobraban hasta 9.000 euros por cruce en pequeñas embarcaciones.
articles.body:
La Policía Nacional ha desarticulado dos organizaciones dedicadas al tráfico ilícito de migrantes entre Ceuta y la península, con cinco detenidos, según ha informado RTVE. Las redes cobraban hasta 9.000 euros por persona por cruzar el Estrecho en pequeñas embarcaciones, y entre los arrestados hay cuatro hombres vinculados a la logística de los cruces, dos en Ceuta y dos en La Línea, además de un patrón.

Una de las investigaciones se centra en un cruce del pasado 14 de agosto en el que siete personas viajaron en una embarcación de cinco metros sin chalecos salvavidas, en una travesía de unas cinco horas y unos cuarenta kilómetros hasta la playa de El Burgo. Los agentes intervinieron también una embarcación rápida varada en Benzú, en Ceuta.

Las pesquisas continúan abiertas y no se descartan nuevas detenciones en el marco de ambas operaciones.

articles.headline: Robbie Butler named as Northern Ireland's new health minister
articles.subtitle: UUP MLA Robbie Butler has been appointed Northern Ireland's health minister, replacing Mike Nesbitt, who resigned last week in a row with party leader Jon Burrows over the Causeway Hospital downgrade plan.
articles.body:
UUP MLA Robbie Butler has been confirmed as Northern Ireland's new health minister, succeeding Mike Nesbitt, who resigned last week in a row with party leader Jon Burrows over the proposed downgrade of services at the Causeway Hospital.

The Lagan Valley MLA, a former deputy leader of the party and a former firefighter, takes over the department that funds his old colleagues in the fire service. Burrows said he was delighted with the appointment and gave Butler no red lines for the role, according to the BBC.

Butler, who has served as the party's health spokesperson, faces immediate pressure over waiting lists, the nurses' pay dispute and the future of the Causeway plan that triggered his predecessor's departure. Opposition parties said the new minister must quickly set out his priorities for the health service.

articles.headline: Foyle Bridge closure criticised after five hours of disruption in Derry
articles.subtitle: Derry's Foyle Bridge was closed for more than five hours on Thursday after a car fire, with politicians criticising the Department for Infrastructure over the disruption and the lack of alternatives for motorists.
articles.body:
The Foyle Bridge in Derry was closed to traffic for more than five hours on Thursday after a car fire, and politicians have criticised the Department for Infrastructure over the disruption.

The bridge shut at about 13:00 BST and reopened shortly after 19:21, after the Northern Ireland Fire and Rescue Service extinguished a fire in a vehicle; the blaze is believed to have been accidental. Motorists faced long queues and detours of up to 30 or 35 miles.

SDLP MLA Mark H. Durkan said the department had failed motorists, DUP MP Gregory Campbell described the impact as unacceptable, and People Before Profit's Shaun Harkin called the disruption a disgrace. The bridge has been under structural inspection since mid-July, with a 30 mph limit and lane closures in place, and its long-term future depends on the North West Transport Plan, which is not due to be completed until 2035.

articles.headline: Man in his 60s dies after house fire in Derry
articles.subtitle: A man in his 60s has died following a fire at a house in the Bloomfield Park area of Galliagh in Derry on Wednesday, with police saying the blaze is not being treated as suspicious.
articles.body:
A man in his 60s has died following a fire at a house in the Bloomfield Park area of Galliagh in Derry on Wednesday afternoon. The Northern Ireland Fire and Rescue Service was called at about 15:42, with five appliances attending the scene, and the man was found inside the property.

He was pronounced dead a short time later. Police have said the fire is not being treated as suspicious, and a post-mortem examination will be carried out to establish the cause of death. The PSNI has appealed for anyone with information or dashcam footage to come forward.

Tributes have been paid locally, with SDLP leader Colum Eastwood expressing his condolences to the man's family and friends and thanking the emergency services for their response.

articles.headline: Russian drone attack on Kryvyi Rih shopping centre kills at least 14
articles.subtitle: A Russian drone strike hit a shopping centre in the central Ukrainian city of Kryvyi Rih, killing at least 14 people and injuring more than a hundred, with rescue teams themselves struck by a second wave of drones.
articles.body:
A Russian drone attack on a shopping centre in the central Ukrainian city of Kryvyi Rih has killed at least 14 people and injured more than a hundred, according to Ukrainian authorities.

The strike hit on Friday evening, and a second wave of drones struck again as rescue teams arrived at the scene, an attack pattern that has drawn international condemnation. Regional officials said children were among the injured, and rescue workers from several regions were deployed to search the rubble.

President Zelensky described the attack as a cynical and cowardly act of terrorism, while the head of the regional administration said the perpetrators were animals. The attack came a day after Russian strikes on Kyiv killed more than a dozen people, and as Ukraine's allies pressed for new air defence support. The UN called for an end to attacks on civilian infrastructure.

articles.headline: Turkey asks Interpol for red notice against Netanyahu over flotilla deaths
articles.subtitle: Turkey's chief prosecutor has asked Interpol to issue a red notice for Benjamin Netanyahu over the deaths of activists on the Sumud flotilla, in the latest escalation of Turkey's legal campaign against Israeli leaders.
articles.body:
Turkey's chief prosecutor has formally asked Interpol to issue a red notice for the arrest of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over the deaths of activists during the 2025 Gaza flotilla, known as Sumud. The request, reported by RTVE and Reuters, is part of a case that an Istanbul court has been pursuing over the incident, which Ankara treats as genocide and other crimes against the flotilla.

The court has already issued arrest warrants for 35 people, and in November 2025 ordered the detention of Netanyahu and 36 others. A red notice is a request to locate and provisionally arrest a person pending extradition, though it is not an international arrest warrant and is not binding on member states.

Israel dismissed the move, with officials calling it pathetic, while Netanyahu has previously described President Erdogan as an antisemitic dictator. The request deepens the confrontation between the two countries, which have been at odds over Gaza since the war began.

articles.headline: Cobalt brings a signed app store and third-party apps to Kobo e-readers
articles.subtitle: Cobalt is an open-source platform that lets Kobo e-readers run apps — a launcher, a signed app store, a Rust SDK and a runtime that keeps every app in its own unprivileged process — installed over USB and updated over Wi-Fi.
articles.body:
Kobo e-readers can now run third-party apps thanks to Cobalt, an open-source application platform that reached the front page of Hacker News this week.

Cobalt consists of a launcher, a signed app store, a Rust SDK and a runtime that keeps every app in its own unprivileged process, so a reboot returns the device to the stock Kobo reader. Installation happens once over USB; after that, apps install, update and remove themselves on the reader over Wi-Fi, with signatures verified before anything launches.

The project's apps include an arXiv reader that paginates papers for the e-ink panel, a Hacker News client, a terminal, an audiobook player and even an app that sends Morse code via the front light. Everything runs on stock hardware, and the project is not affiliated with Rakuten Kobo.

articles.headline: US citizen faces felony charges for deleting phone data during border search
articles.subtitle: The New York Times reports that a US citizen, Samuel Tunick, faces felony charges for deleting his phone's data during a border search, a case that has alarmed civil liberties groups and topped Hacker News.
articles.body:
A US citizen is facing felony charges after deleting his phone's data during a search by border agents, according to The New York Times.

The case of Samuel Tunick, which drew hundreds of comments on Hacker News, centres on whether wiping a device during a border inspection can expose a traveller to criminal prosecution. A federal judge in Florida ruled that Tunick can be charged after he allegedly deleted the contents of his phone while it was being examined.

The decision has alarmed privacy advocates, who warn it could criminalise a routine precaution and chill legitimate privacy protections at the border. Lawyers for Tunick argue the deletion was a reasonable step to protect personal data and that the prosecution sets a dangerous precedent. The case is being watched closely by civil liberties organisations as it works its way through the courts.

articles.headline: Grok users report gibberish responses as xAI confirms a generation glitch
articles.subtitle: Users of xAI's Grok chatbot on Grok.com reported receiving streams of gibberish this week, with the company confirming a rare temporary generation glitch, days after reports that xAI has lost much of its founding team.
articles.body:
Users of xAI's Grok chatbot on Grok.com reported receiving gibberish responses this week, with threads on Reddit showing replies of broken text and nonsensical fragments. TechCrunch reported that the glitch appeared to affect a subset of users, possibly on the lighter Grok Lite tier, while responses on X itself were unaffected.

An xAI staff account confirmed it was a rare temporary generation glitch and said the issue had been resolved, though the company's status page had listed all services as operational. The company pointed users to the feedback channel for further reports.

The incident comes at a delicate moment for xAI: The Information reported that the company has lost more than 50 researchers this year, including most of its founding team, raising questions about the pace of development of Grok 4.5 and its successors.

articles.headline: Meta launches an AI assistant Mac app with system-wide dictation and screen context
articles.subtitle: Meta's new AI assistant for Mac brings system-wide dictation and on-screen context to the desktop, letting it draft documents, manage business accounts and answer questions about what is on screen, taking on Google's Gemini.
articles.body:
Meta has launched a standalone AI assistant app for Mac that combines system-wide dictation with screen context, letting the assistant see and act on what the user is looking at.

The app, reported by TechCrunch, uses a model codenamed Muse Spark to understand on-screen content, and can draft emails and documents, summarise pages and answer questions about anything visible on the display. For business users, it can manage Instagram and Facebook accounts, run ad campaigns, pull data from Google Workspace and even prepare competitor intelligence and proposal decks.

The launch follows Google's Gemini app for Mac, which added dictation last month, and puts Meta in direct competition with dictation startups such as Wispr Flow and Superwhisper. Meta has been pushing AI into its enterprise tools under Mark Zuckerberg, with its WhatsApp Business AI agent rolling out globally in June.

articles.headline: A third of web pages published since ChatGPT's launch show signs of AI authorship
articles.subtitle: A Pew Research Center analysis of pages from Common Crawl finds that about 35% of web pages published after ChatGPT's launch show signs of AI-generated text, roughly ten times the rate of earlier pages.
articles.body:
Roughly a third of web pages published since ChatGPT launched in late 2022 show signs of AI-generated text, according to a new analysis by the Pew Research Center.

Researchers examined hundreds of thousands of English-language pages from Common Crawl spanning the past five years, using an AI-detection tool called Open Pangram. About 35% of pages published after ChatGPT's debut showed signs of AI authorship, while in a random sample of 10,000 pages published in July 2026, roughly 10% contained significant amounts of AI-generated text.

Commercial sites were hardest hit: pages on .com domains were roughly ten times more likely to show AI signs than .edu or .gov pages, with .org at around 4.6%. The study notes that AI text tends to carry tell-tale signs such as em dashes and Oxford commas, and arrives as Cloudflare data shows bots overtaking humans in web traffic for the first time.
